runs.name: HMH Holding Inc.; NYSE HMH Class A, drilling equipment, spare parts, aftermarket services and digital solutions for onshore and offshore oil and gas drilling and for mining, operational centers in Houston and Kristiansand; HMH B.V. formed 2021-10-01 from Akastor's MHWirth and Baker Hughes's Subsea Drilling Systems; initial public offering closed 2026-04-02 at $20.00 in an Up-C structure, Baker Hughes and Akastor holding all the Class B; a resale S-1 for 31,891,652 Class A shares filed 2026-09-28; no 10-K yet; NOV, Nabors and SLB read as the filers among the rivals the prospectus names
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$17.34** (2026-10-15 close, through `tools/sources.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **44,093,153**, both classes counted (Class A 12,201,501 and Class B 31,891,652 at 2026-09-28, resale S-1 0001193125-26-405527; each Class B share travels with B.V. units redeemable for one Class A share, so both carry one equal economic unit of the operating company; cross-checked against the 10-Q cover and issued less treasury); cap **$764.6M**; net debt **$78.1M** at 2026-06-30 (debt $197.8M less cash $119.7M; operating leases and the $3.8M TRA liability left out, said so). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: no 10-K exists (listed 2026-04-02); the 424B4 (0001193125-26-138102) with FY2024 and FY2025 audited statements, the first S-1 (0001193125-24-198984) for FY2022 and FY2023, the Q2 2026 10-Q (0001628280-26-053385), the 8-K of 2026-08-05 and its release, the item list of the 8-K of 2026-04-02, the resale S-1; no proxy filed; one figure cross-checked (six-month operating cash $25,156K, 10-Q against XBRL). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the prospectus's Business, Risk factors and MD&A and the 10-Qs (the brief's departure, no 10-K existing), stated in the run file. `tools/run.py` returned nothing for the filer; every figure taken by hand. Only four year-ends of balance sheets (2022 to 2025) and four years of statements exist; read in Step 0: goodwill and intangibles $443M of $1,294M of assets at 2022 from the 2021 formation, tangible equity $124M to $271M, working capital absorbing $183M over 2022 to 2025 (inventories up, payables, accruals and customer prepayments down), debt about $340M to the IPO and $198M after. Q1 IN (PCS and the aftermarket readable; one of three full-package suppliers with NOV and SLB's Cameron; recertification by the maker under US and European regulators). **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: the deciding part, PCS (pressure control, 67.6% of 2022 to 2025 segment profit, 77% aftermarket), has a real castle in its certified installed base of about 1,100 installations, but no filing shows its returns through an offshore downturn: HMH B.V. was formed in October 2021 and no predecessor statements are filed; the field's rig segments lost money or earned little 2016 to 2021 (NOV's rig segments about 21% to 23% in 2014 to 2015, losses most years 2016 to 2021; Nabors's Canrig losses 2017 to 2020; SLB 9% to 16% on a mixed segment) while NOV's separately reported aftermarket arm still earned 16.2% in 2016; PCS margin 7.6% to 20.3% over 2022 to 2025; the filer says it must be "aggressive on pricing to secure work" in its main market; 210 floaters retired since 2010, 173 left, no newbuild orders since 2014; revenue -2.6% in FY2025 and -14.9% in H1 2026, products -53.1%. The recent returns read as a change for the better, credited only on a full cycle. Re-look: the FY2026 10-K, then each falling year until a full cycle is on file. Huisman, KCA Deutag, Worldwide Oilfield Machine, Drillmec, Honghua and Rongsheng flagged as non-filers. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** material weaknesses in internal control in Q4 2023 (four) and in 2025 (revenue cutoff in subsidiaries in certain regions), each reported remediated; Q2 2026 "Free Cash Flow" of $22.2M reported above operating cash flow of $17.9M; about $190M of the $211M IPO proceeds reaching Baker Hughes and Akastor (share purchase and shareholder-loan repayment), who keep about 72% of the vote; pre-IPO stock awards of $22.8M expensed only at the IPO. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: four-year window (a CONVENTION of the run, five years not existing), owner cash all-equity after acquisitions $(8.0)M, $15.4M, $8.7M, $82.5M for 2022 to 2025, average $24.7M (the pre-IPO awards spread over 2022 to 2025 and a 25% interest shield, each a CONVENTION of the run); the halves rate of 249% cut by specific (f) to the business's sales growth and then to the discount rate; value **$8.53 to $14.13** a share all-equity against $17.34, the price above the top, return at the price 2.9% to 4.6%, no case earning the floor; fair price **$5.09 all-equity**, equity-only not positive on the interest filed ($(1.46)), $3.58 on today's bonds (a CONVENTION of the run); beside, not chosen: $17.83 with no working-capital draw; not armed, the box being TOO HARD at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: the NOV fold commit subjects seen in its opening context, not used (rival figures from its own reading on segment margins); a name filter for "HMH" on the `Test Runs/` listing at the start, no match. Commits daf6111f, e2bad7e2, efce3a69, 345dd370, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for HMH, MHWirth or Akastor). Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` PASS (39 ids); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 10 quotation-and-id pairs, no missing id, no slip; the wider sweep's misses are filing quotations and section names, none beside a ledger row's words. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) a newly listed company with four filed years against Q7's five and Q4's eight to ten; (2) the change-for-the-better re-look condition is met literally by a 2.6% dip; (3) whether the field's returns are the rivals' whole segment or the part matching the deciding part; (4) working capital moving the fair price from $5 to $18 on a carve-out's balance-sheet rebuild; (5) how to count an Up-C class with no economic rights at the issuer; (6) whether a knowable non-SEC record of a non-deciding part (Akastor's Oslo filings for MHWirth) makes a research pass worth writing. Could not get: a fifth year, any filed downturn record for PCS, the rivals' segment capital, a proxy.
runs.narr: Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): the deciding part, PCS (pressure control, 67.6% of 2022 to 2025 segment profit, 77% aftermarket), has a real castle in a certified installed base, but HMH B.V. was formed in October 2021 and no filing shows its returns through an offshore downturn; the field's rig segments lost money or earned little 2016 to 2021; the filer says it must be aggressive on pricing to secure work; 210 floaters retired since 2010 with no newbuild orders since 2014. Re-look: the FY2026 10-K. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: material weaknesses in 2023 and 2025, reported remediated; a free cash flow figure above operating cash flow; most IPO proceeds to Baker Hughes and Akastor. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $8.53 to $14.13 all-equity against $17.34, fair $5.09 all-equity (equity-only not positive on filed interest), not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: windows for a newly listed company; the size of fall the re-look condition means; the field for a business of parts; working capital in a carve-out; the Up-C share count.
